---
title: "Methods and data sources"
---

## Glider data

The deployments are gridded (L3) NetCDF files produced by the NOAA Southwest Fisheries
Science Center (SWFSC) Ecosystem Science Division Glider Team with
[pyglider](https://github.com/c-proof/pyglider) and
[esdglider](https://github.com/SWFSC/esdglider)
([glider lab manual](https://swfsc.github.io/glider-lab-manual/)). Each file holds one
profile per column on 5 m depth bins, with one time, latitude and longitude per profile.
The data are in the public domain (CC0-1.0).

Values are shown as stored. The gridded QC flags are bin-averaged in these files, so they
are not used for masking. Potential density in the files was computed from raw,
uncorrected salinity.

## What the viewer shows

**3D curtain.** The selected variable on a vertical surface beneath the glider track,
in km east/north of the deployment's mean position. Vertical exaggeration is adjustable;
land heights are scaled down so islands do not hide the curtain.

**Depth–time section.** The same variable against time and depth, with the seafloor
under the track, labelled σθ contours (lightly smoothed along time for display), and a
sun strip showing day, civil twilight, nautical twilight and night for each profile.

**T–S diagram.** Potential temperature against practical salinity for the selected date
window, with σθ isopycnals computed from the EOS-80 equation of state (Millero & Poisson
1981). EOS-80 matches the files' potential density to within about 0.006 kg m⁻³ and is
used only to draw the isopycnals.

## Derived quantities

**Mixed-layer depth** — the depth where σθ first exceeds its value at 10 m by
0.03 kg m⁻³ (de Boyer Montégut et al. 2004), interpolated between bins. Left blank where
a profile has no data in the top 15 m or never crosses the threshold.

**Chlorophyll-maximum depth** — the depth of the largest chlorophyll value in the upper
300 m after a 3-bin running mean, for profiles with data starting within 20 m of the surface.
Daytime chlorophyll fluorescence near the surface is reduced by non-photochemical quenching
(Xing et al. 2012), so daytime maxima can appear deeper than they are; compare with night
profiles using the sun strip.

Both lines are drawn as 7-profile running medians. The readout gives each profile's own value.

**Sun elevation** — computed for each profile's time and position with the low-precision
solar formulae of the Astronomical Almanac (no refraction). Classes: day > −0.833°,
civil twilight to −6°, nautical twilight to −12°, night below.

## Bathymetry and land

GEBCO Compilation Group (2026) *GEBCO_2026 Grid*, 15 arc-second,
doi:[10.5285/4f68d5c7-45eb-f999-e063-7086abc036fa](https://doi.org/10.5285/4f68d5c7-45eb-f999-e063-7086abc036fa).
Seafloor depth under the track is the nearest grid cell; the 3D surface is thinned for
speed. GEBCO is partly interpolated away from survey lines and is not for navigation.

## Colour maps

cmocean perceptually uniform colour maps (Thyng et al. 2016): *thermal* for temperature,
*haline* for salinity, *algae* for chlorophyll (log scale by default), *deep* for oxygen.
